headline: Recommended approval of North Pkwy. crosswalks, Gage St. one-way, Bristol St. No Parking zone, and Wamsutta Ave. permit parking removal; many others recommended for filing.
summary: Items covered crosswalks, traffic signs, speed, parking, and one-way street changes. It recommended approval for North Pkwy. crosswalks, a one-way Gage St., a No Parking zone on Bristol St., and removal of Wamsutta Ave. resident permit parking. It recommended filing most other petitions and held the Thorne St. one-way petition.

. Virtual Attendee Call-In Information/Important Notice to Petitioners 1 
Pursuant to Chapter 20 of the Acts of 2021 and in order to ensure active, public 
engagement, the City of Worcester currently allows for both in -person and remote 
participation at all City Council and Standing Committee meetings. To partake in the 
meeting, you may attend the meeting in -person within the meeting location, follow the 
below link to join via Zoom or dial the direct line as indicated. If you join a Zoom 
meeting by dialing in with a phone number, you can raise your hand by dialing *9.
Traffic and Parking Committee Zoom Link:
https://worcesterma.zoomgov.com/j/1614119888
Traffic and Parking Committee Zoom Phone Number: +1 646 828 7666
Traffic and Parking Committee Zoom Access Code: 161 411 9888
a.
Important Notice: Please be aware our office has been notified of an ongoing scam 
involving the impersonation of city officials and departments. Scammers are fraudulently 
requesting payments be made for planning and zoning permits, as well as City Council 
petitions. All official emails regarding your petition will come exclusively from an 
@worcesterma.gov email address (such as clerk @worcesterma.gov), or via physical mail 
on the City of Worcester’s official letterhead. Any legitimate hearing letter will always 
include your specific application details, along with the scheduled hearing date, time, 
and location. The City of Worcester will never request payments via wire transfer.
b.

# 10q CC August 19, 2025
a.
Chairperson Councilor Rivera read the item and recognized the following Speakers:
1. Brian Thamel, Worcester resident, spoke in favor of the item
Chairperson Councilor Rivera recognized the Commissioner of Transportation and Mobility, who 
provided the recommendation to file, as the location cannot be made safe for pedestrian crossing 
with pavement markings and a Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacon (RRFB) due to the motor 
vehicle speeds, volume, and crash history; the establishment of a safe midblock crossing in this 
vicinity would require roadway redesign and construction and the safest option is to utilize the 
crosswalk at Chandler St. to travel between the parking lot and building on the opposite side of 
the street.
Chairperson Councilor Rivera recognized Councilor Ojeda, who discussed concerns related to 
speeding in the area and traffic calming methods to address traffic issues.
Chairperson Councilor Rivera moved for a roll call vote to accept the recommendation.
Recommend File on a roll call vote of 3 Yeas and 0 Nays
